correctness.rationale: Exact two-step noise cancellation gives Y_next=A^2 Y+q ξ with q=r(b-r,1) and iid symmetric signs. Strict Jury conditions 1-b>0, r>0, and 2(1+b)-r>0 give Schur stability, a unique stationary covariance, and decay of any deterministic start. All entries of an explicit symmetric covariance matrix satisfy the discrete Lyapunov equation by symbolic identity; the iid comparison uses its own Lyapunov equation. Taking explicit limits proves the separate r^3 and r^2 powers and the uniform b≈sqrt(r) crossover. The embedded checker additionally passed 30 fully enumerated exact-rational covariance comparisons and five independently iterated numerical recurrences; those finite checks corroborate rather than replace the infinite-time proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp stationary heavy-ball random-reshuffling covariance and its jointly singular b≈sqrt(r) crossover are not direct instances of the accessible claims in the 2024 RRM, SMG, RR, and independent-noise momentum literature. Targeted alias, exact-parameter, and broad-coverage comparisons did not identify a dominating statement. Generic Schur/Lyapunov mathematics is prior art and is explicitly not claimed new; the specific completed-epoch versus intermediate-phase decomposition and its asymptotic boundary supply the original component. Search cannot establish uniqueness, and equivalent older switching-system formulas remain a concrete residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2022 Domingo-Enrich momentum-reshuffling variance paper is exceptionally close; its available author code reports all-step averages and does not give phase decomposition, but the inaccessible full text might contain a stronger phase-resolved statement.
Unindexed or inaccessible older momentum/reshuffling analyses may use a dual parametrization, or a later full version may subsume the special asymptotic.
Applicability does not extend to arbitrary finite sums, general Hessian spectra, or within-epoch averages.

value.rationale: The smallest noninterpolating strongly convex random reshuffling objective exposes how memory transports a within-epoch random gradient into the next epoch and changes the ratio of phase variances. The exact parameter transition b=O(sqrt(r)) needed to preserve the cubic epoch-end noise-floor power distinguishes fixed, vanishing, and zero momentum and gives a concrete tuning boundary. The phase-specific intermediate-step variance and with-replacement comparator quantify the remaining noise and the retained variance-reduction benefit, so the statement answers a natural algorithmic question rather than reporting an unmotivated numerical value. Limitations to this phase and model are clearly acknowledged.
